catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds the LI-COR scan-console start, pause, stop and cancel commands. cap.motion.stop.v1 is for robot, mobile-base and motion-axis resources and has a deceleration input; it does not carry pausing or resuming a scanner. The package uses an x-cap id with an inline command enum.
catalogue_requests.summary: Start, pause, stop or cancel the configured Odyssey scan through command.pl.

catalogue_requests.reason: The vendor's status-page Stop is the scanner's documented release path, but no catalogue class binds it as a safe-state action on a sensor.camera resource. cap.motion.stop.v1 is motion-resource specific and carries no safe-state semantics for this endpoint.
catalogue_requests.summary: Stop the scanner through the status-page Stop command; the e-stop and the runtime safe-state path both call it.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PyLabRobotDriver helper (family pylabrobot), but the Odyssey front end is not a PyLabRobot LiquidHandler and the device is a scanner/imager. The helper's own guide sends other PyLabRobot machines to a direct Driver, so this package is a direct Driver over the card's transport entry class plr_v4.odyssey.connection:OdysseyDriver (connection.py:223). No native wire syntax or interface shape was changed. native.py is the hardware adapter; it imports the pinned upstream transport and converts the driver's plain configuration mapping to ScanParameters. The fake is .fake:FakeOdyssey and never imports or runs the clone.

COVERED: cap.device.configure.v1 writes for scan name, group, resolution, quality, both intensity values, both channel enables, origin X/Y, width, height and focus, sent together to configure.pl and followed by the full seven-step initializing.pl poll (connection.py:360-485); reads of scanner state, progress, time remaining, current user, lid status, instrument information and the next configuration; x-cap.vcjdeboer.odyssey_control_scan.v1 for start, pause, stop and cancel through command.pl (connection.py:487-525); cap.sensing.image.v1 for the instrument-rendered JPEG preview as a bounded image/jpeg artifact, with actual frame width and height parsed from the JPEG start-of-frame segment; x-cap.vcjdeboer.odyssey_safe_stop.v1 and @estop for the status-page Stop command (connection.py:568-578). The raw TIFF path is not exposed.

STOP AND SAFETY: the @estop method and the safe_state action both call OdysseyDriver.stop_from_status; the hardware adapter bounds that POST to two seconds so an unreachable instrument cannot hold the e-stop for the transport's default sixty-second timeout, and a timeout or error is reported as a failed safe state, never as a stopped scanner. This is a vendor HTTP stop command, not a certified emergency stop; the clone documents no independent hardware e-stop and does not state a laser class. Risk is R2, chosen conservatively from the 80 mW 685 nm and 785 nm diode lasers recorded in the device card (device_card.py:26-40) and the scanner motion; the card floor is R1. The driver does not claim a hardware lid interlock; the device card declares one and the driver only reads the status-page lid state.

NOT COVERED: raw TIFF channel downloads (connection.py:601-657), the imaging progress page (connection.py:580-597), the scan log and group/preset listing, the administrator shutdown, the low-intensity L-prefixed settings, and the upstream simulator. The image action covers the JPEG preview, not the 16-bit raw TIFF channels; a raw TIFF would be an opaque artifact without the calibration and metadata the app adds. The image class inputs are constrained to what the preview endpoint can honor: camera selects 700, 800 or both; format is jpeg; width and height must equal the actual rendered preview; exposure_ms must be 0 because the preview endpoint has no exposure control. width_cm and height_cm are operator_required because the clone states only origin + size <= 25 cm and no minimum or site maximum; the image width, height and exposure are operator_required for the same reason. site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a property of an installed unit.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: the fake returns a placeholder 8 x 6 JPEG, canned progress and instrument information, and a small state machine. It accepts scan commands without enforcing the instrument's configure-before-start rule and does not model the two raw channels, motion, timing, optics or the real preview size; those are fidelity gaps, not device facts. No hardware was attached and no upstream simulator was run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null. The gate run was on the fake backend only and establishes contract_checked evidence, never an MHS-Device level, a hardware run or a ROS run. The final gate run had no warnings. The Fact list is split so each cited line shows its own statement; the package decisions (not using the upstream simulator and not claiming an independent hardware interlock) are recorded in facts.md and these notes.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation (the Odyssey is an HTTP-CGI imager, not a PyLabRobot LiquidHandler, as the readiness evidence said), every fact and limit against connection.py, device_card.py and status_backend.py, the image capture and the stop. The stop is a real upstream command (stop_from_status, the upstream's force_stop), but it returns the response text unchecked (connection.py:568-578), so the @estop and the safe_state=True action reported a completed stop for any returned POST, error pages included; the upstream's own stop_and_save confirms a stop by polling the status page for idle or stopped for up to 15 s (scan_backend.py:38, 103-117). The reviewer made both stop paths read the status page after the Stop and fail MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED unless it reports Idle or Stopped (the safe-stop output adds the state), rewrote safe_state, said when progress_percent is a placeholder 0.0, extended one fact and added two (driver.py, facts.md), added a stop_ignored switch (fake.py) and two cases, a confirmed stop during a scan and an unconfirmed stop that stays latched (test_driver.py), and regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md; gate and strict collector pass, digest unchanged (sha256:d47f6618a7b801a0b35b14783a079815f79c85a0429c6b6c1976b79b1a867210). For the human reviewer: Two 80 mW diode lasers (685 and 785 nm) inside an instrument with a lid interlock and a moving scan head; the author's R2 is kept. The instrument may need up to 15 s to show Idle after a Stop, so the first e-stop attempt can be reported unreached and is retried; lid, lasers and queued firmware work are not confirmed. Configure writes run the seven-step initializing.pl countdown that prepares motors and lasers. Credentials come from ODYSSEY_USER and ODYSSEY_PASS.
